title: NodeJS Internals & Architecture
summary: In this course I gained deep insight into the internals of NodeJS - Libuv, V8, Event Loop Phases, Threads, Processes, OS communication, I/O operations.
bullets: Event Loop Mechanics: Reviewed and learned the internal phases of the Node.js Event Loop (Initial, Timers, Pending, Poll, Check, Close) and microtask queues (process.nextTick, Promises). I saw examples and analyzed how blocking the main thread causes callback starvation and dropped server requests.

Asynchronous I/O & Libuv: Gained insight into Libuv. Di erentiated between non-blocking operations delegated directly to the OS (network I/O) and operations o loaded to the Libuv thread pool (File System, DNS lookups).

Worker Threads: Learned how to spot CPU intensive operations and how to use the worker threads module in order to o load CPU intensive operations to another thread and prevent blocking of the main one.
Process Management: Evaluated the architectural tradeo s between scaling Child Processes (memory isolation, IPC) and Worker Threads (shared memory) for high-performance backend applications.

title: OOP Design Patterns
summary:
In this course I got to know what a Design Pattern is, why were they created and why are they used. I learned the main Design Principles which every developer and Design Pattern tries to follow, these principles are:

 1. Programming To An Interface
 2. Composition Over Inheritance
 3. Delegation
 4. Single Responsibility
 5. Open Closed
 6. Liskov Substitution
 7. Interface Segregation
 8. Dependency Inversion
 9. Dependency Injection

 After the main principles I learned the 3 types of patterns - Creational, Structural and Behavioural.

 The Creational patterns I now know are: Factory Method, Abstract Factory Method, Singleton, Builder and Prototype.
 The Structural patterns I now know are: Adapter, Bridge, Composite, Decorator, Facade, Flyweight and Proxy.
 The Behavioural patterns I now know are: Chain of Responsibility, Command, Interpreter, Iterator, Mediator, Memento, Observer, State, Strategy, Template Method and Visitor.
